candidates.buyer: Legal entities and sole entrepreneurs that take or discharge water from water bodies for business use: bottled-water plants, fish farms and aquaculture, greenhouses and farms with wells, car-wash and small industrial users, spa and resort operators. Natural persons meeting their own needs and landowners drilling a first unconfined-aquifer well on their own land for their own needs are exempt.
candidates.category: 13. Small water systems (adjacent: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction)
candidates.evidence: https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/aze244107.pdf (full text read: sections 1-4 and the permit form); https://www.nk.gov.az/uploads/doc/docs/69de426b8d00e.pdf (Decision 99: fees, contract form, in force 1 Sep 2026). The fee figures come from a search summary and were not read in the annex.
candidates.existing: No dedicated software found. The competitor search 'su obyektlərindən xüsusi istifadə icazə proqram xidməti məsləhət quyu icazəsi sahibkarlar ... ASAN' returned only the legal texts and the list of business permits. The application goes to the Agency on paper or through the administrative-procedure channel, and some data is pulled automatically from e-government (rule 2.3). Local consultants or ecology firms may sell the application as a service; this was not checked.
candidates.name: Special-purpose water-use permit, contract and fee compliance for businesses (Decree 554 / Cabinet Decision 99)
candidates.trigger: Presidential Decree 554 of 18 Dec 2025 approved the 'Procedure for issuing permits for special-purpose use of water bodies' under Water Code art. 34. Permits are issued by the State Water Resources Agency on the basis of a permit plus a water-use contract, with a state duty. Cabinet Decision 99 of 14 Apr 2026 set the use fees and the contract form, in force 1 Sep 2026. The application needs coordinates, equipment capacity, forecast demand (thousand m3 per year or month), treatment capacity, discharge limits and the latest water-use statistics report. Supervision is by the State Service for Water Use and Protection, and inspections are tied to the unified inspection register. Permits are issued within the Water Code art. 32 terms. Fee examples reported by search: 0.01 AZN per m3 for domestic or drinking use on rivers and lakes; aquaculture discharge at a 10x coefficient.
candidates.unchecked: Number of affected firms and how many already hold permits. Permit validity and renewal cycle (Water Code art. 32 was not read). Whether metering and periodic water-use reporting to the Agency is required (the statistics form, apparently '2-tp (su)', was not confirmed). Fee annex contents. Whether the Agency has an e-portal. Enforcement news since 1 Sep 2026. Mostly a one-off or multi-year permit, so recurring pain may be low and buyers are scattered across industries.

candidates.name: Bottled-water (19 L) producers: AFSA food-safety records and sample compliance
candidates.trigger: AFSA monitoring and unplanned inspections. In Aug 2025 a sampled 19 L batch from a natural person's plant in Sumgait failed, and the inspection found that temperature monitoring and records were not kept, no ventilation was installed, and cleaning was not done. AFSA registers food-safety operators.
candidates.unchecked: Number of bottlers, water-source analysis frequency, any separate water-quality rules for bottled water.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No quiet-business buyer found for small drinking-water systems themselves. Rural and small supply is run by state bodies: Azersu and the Regional Water Melioration Service sit under the State Water Resources Agency (Decree 2074 of 2023; Cabinet statute 2024). Azersu's 'Large Cities Water Supply' was reorganised by Decree 600 of 20 Feb 2026. No law or register for community-managed or private small drinking-water systems turned up, and the WUA material found is irrigation only (belongs to the farm side). Two adjacent angles were found: (1) a new permit and contract regime for special-purpose use of water bodies, Presidential Decree 554 of 18 Dec 2025 plus Cabinet Decision 99 of 14 Apr 2026, in force 1 Sep 2026; (2) AFSA enforcement against a small bottled-water producer in Sumgait (Aug 2025). Searches in Azerbaijani, Russian and English. Sources: https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/aze244107.pdf (Decree 554, text read via pdftotext); https://www.nk.gov.az/uploads/doc/docs/69de426b8d00e.pdf (Cabinet Decision 99, text read); https://afsa.gov.az/storage/pages/11438/sumqayitda-su-emali-muessisesinde-uygunsuzlugun-askarlanmasina-dair-melumat-20-avqust-2025.pdf (PDF unreadable via WebFetch, so only the search snippet was used). Not checked: the fee annex to Decision 99 (not extracted), the Water Code text, and Cabinet Decision 111 of 2000 on individual wells (current status unconfirmed).

result.reason: The AQTA Collegium Decision No. 19 on vet pharmacy organisation and operation exists as a FAOLEX entry. A later AQTA decision No. 37 (20 Sep 2023) lists the same title, so Decision 19 may have been amended or replaced. I could not read the text (FAOLEX returned 403), so record-keeping duties, inspection frequency and penalties are unconfirmed. I found no electronic reporting system for vet drug sales and no vet-pharmacy software (about 4 searches, no dedicated vendor search). The market is probably small, likely a few hundred outlets, but I found no register count. A weak recurring workflow with an unclear mandate. Score stays at 3.

Duty is real: employers file next-year foreign-labour forecast with the State Migration Service by 1 May via ASAN imza, and work permits are 1 year and must be renewed at least 30 days before expiry (migration.gov.az/en/page/75). The state e-service already handles filing, and no third-party software was found. Weaknesses: the duty is a low-volume filing, so there are few small employers and little recurring pain. Fees are state-set, and the work is easily done by lawyers or recruiters. No penalty figure or employer count was found, and the Fragomen page returned 403, so I used search summaries for the 1 May deadline. Overlaps category 26.

A duty exists: a 2018 Financial Markets Supervision Chamber rule on supervising licensed exchange activity requires periodic reports in a set form and deadline. Decision 59/2025 (capital AZN 300-600k, monthly and annual reports, AML) is seen only in a secondary summary. The cbar.az and regalert pages returned 429 or unreadable PDFs. I found no office count, no penalty detail, and no confirmation of the reporting channel (likely a central bank system). Competitor search turned up no dedicated software, but nothing was confirmed either way. Few, well-capitalised buyers, central-bank-prescribed systems and a niche market make a solo-founder product unattractive. Score kept low.

Decision No. 68 (10 Mar 2025) exists and sets quality requirements for state and non-state child institutions under art. 29-1 of the Law on Children's Rights. It amends the model kindergarten charter so kindergartens operate under it (search summary). I could not read the full text, because the PDF was unreadable. I found no recurring reporting duty, inspection frequency or penalty. It looks like a one-off standard rather than a recurring filing workflow. I found no private kindergarten count. Official figures cover only 1,676 state kindergartens, and 63 private grant recipients is the only private-sector number. I ran no competitor search and found no software. The buyer pool is small and the pain is unproven.

result.competitor: No private AML software found for realtors. State free ŞƏMS reporting platform (Tax Service/FMS) covers the reporting part.
result.duty: Law 781-VIQ of 30 Dec 2022: internal control programme, customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting to FMS. Penalties not found.
result.market: About 2,271 obliged persons registered on ŞƏMS under the Tax Service (all types, not only realtors). Realtor count not found.
result.reason: Duty is real: Law 781-VIQ (30 Dec 2022) binds realtors and other DNFBPs to an internal control programme, customer due diligence and suspicious-transaction reporting to the FMS. The State Tax Service supervises realtors, and its guidance (taxes.gov.az Tələblər.docx) explains the duties. It also says 2,271 obliged persons are registered on the state ŞƏMS reporting platform, so a free state reporting channel exists. I found no private AML software for realtors. MONEYVAL 2023 found no real-estate supervision in its review period and weak sanctions, so enforcement pressure and willingness to pay are low. Fine amounts were not found. The 2,271 figure covers all obliged persons at State Tax Service, not realtors alone. The buyer group is small and informal. Notaries and lawyers are supervised by other bodies.

Duty is real: Decree 554 (18 Dec 2025) sets the special-purpose water-use permit. Cabinet Decision 99 (14 Apr 2026, in force 1 Sep 2026) sets fees and the contract form. Search summaries gave rates: drinking 0.01 AZN/m3, industrial 0.04, agriculture 0.001, with a 0.7 reduction for treated discharge. I couldn't read the PDF annex, so these rates are unconfirmed. Contract fields include monthly volumes, so periodic reporting is likely. No dedicated software was found, and no agency e-portal was confirmed. Weaknesses: the permit is mostly one-off, fees are tiny, buyers are scattered across industries, and the count of firms is unknown (not found). Farmers are complaining. Low willingness to pay, so a low score.
